title: The Last Crumb
background: At dawn, Maribel Crust reopened her beloved bakery after a costly renovation, inviting five people who had helped build its reputation. The next morning, Maribel was found dead beneath the flour mill in the locked basement, with a shard of the bakery's new green display tile beside her. Police discovered that the murder occurred during the brief pre-opening rush.
key_evidence: The florist's outdoor security camera records Elian Voss's distinctive blue delivery van parked behind the bakery from 5:38 to 5:56 a.m., directly contradicting any claim that he was making his supposed delivery across town during that interval. The bakery's rear-door log shows that Elian's access card opened the door at 5:41 a.m.

Elian Voss.motive: Maribel had discovered he was overcharging the bakery and planned to cancel his contract.

Tessa Crust.role: Maribel's younger sister and pastry chef
Tessa Crust.motive: Maribel intended to sell the bakery, leaving Tessa without her livelihood.

Jonah Bell.motive: Maribel had blamed him for the reopening's failed first batch and threatened to fire him.

Priya Nand.motive: Maribel refused to pay the final renovation invoice after publicly accusing Priya of wasting money.

Calder Wynn.motive: Maribel knew Calder had accepted secret payments from competing restaurants for negative reviews.

Nell Oram.motive: Maribel had caught Nell stealing small amounts from the register and planned to report her.

statements.Priya Nand: At 5:41 a.m., I was at the town library photocopying the renovation plans. The library machine recorded that copying session while I prepared the documents connected to Maribel’s project.

title: The Crimson Misattribution
background: At the opening of the Halcyon Gallery's new exhibition, a staged break-in sends guests rushing toward the loading dock. Gallery owner Lucan Vey is found dead beside a shattered display case in the east gallery at 9:27 p.m., killed by a blow from a bronze sculpture. The apparent burglary has left several valuable works untouched, suggesting the theft was a cover for murder.
key_evidence: The east-gallery security camera, whose clock was independently synchronized with the building's fire alarm system, records Ivo Venn entering the gallery at 9:17 p.m. and remaining there until 9:21 p.m.; this directly disproves the loading-dock alibi he later gives.

Ivo Venn.motive: Lucan had discovered that Ivo was secretly replacing authentic works with forged ones and planned to report him.

Mara Quill.relationship_to_victim: Artist whose exhibition Lucan was hosting
Mara Quill.motive: Lucan intended to cancel her show after learning she had fabricated parts of her artistic résumé.

Tamsin Roe.relationship_to_victim: Former partner in a failed gallery venture
Tamsin Roe.motive: Lucan had taken credit for her security designs and ruined her professional reputation.

Dorian Pike.motive: Lucan was blackmailing him with proof that several pieces in his collection had been illegally exported.

Celeste Aran.motive: Lucan had fired her that afternoon and threatened to expose her diversion of promotional funds.

Bram Sallow.relationship_to_victim: Contractor who delivered the exhibition pieces
Bram Sallow.motive: Lucan had withheld payment and blamed Bram for a damaged shipment.

statements.Bram Sallow: At 9:18 p.m., I was outside the loading dock helping a gallery porter secure an empty crate. We were occupied with the shipment area as the guests rushed out, and I did not enter the east gallery.

title: The Lake House Alibi
background: The Vale family gathers at their aging lake house to decide what to do with its dwindling inheritance. Matriarch Beatrice Vale is found dead in the library at 9:45 p.m., an antique fireplace poker beside her and rainwater streaking the open French doors. A storm has cut the road off from town, leaving the family trapped together.
key_evidence: The boathouse security camera has an unbroken, time-stamped recording of Mara Vale inside the boathouse office from 9:16 to 9:24 p.m., and the only door is visible throughout. Therefore Mara could not have been in the library when Beatrice was killed at 9:20 p.m.

Mara Vale.motive: Beatrice had discovered Mara was secretly diverting money from the family trust.

Jonah Vale.role: Beatrice's younger son and fishing-guide business owner
Jonah Vale.motive: Beatrice planned to sell the lake property, which Jonah's livelihood depended on.

Priya Vale.motive: Beatrice intended to disinherit Priya after learning she had forged letters for a bestselling family memoir.

Caleb Rusk.motive: Beatrice had threatened to dismiss him and expose his theft of antique fixtures.

Elise Vale.motive: Beatrice had blocked Elise from receiving any share of her late husband's inheritance.

Theo Vale.role: Beatrice's youngest grandson and aspiring musician
Theo Vale.motive: Beatrice refused to fund Theo's recording project and had mocked him publicly that evening.

statements.Theo Vale: At 9:20 p.m., I was in the boathouse loft recording a song on my phone. The recording captures the storm’s thunder throughout, and I stayed upstairs until it ended.

title: The Quiet Signal

Company founder Soren Bell is found dead at 10:16 p.m. inside the locked prototype lab, killed by a blow from a heavy microphone component. A storm has cut the lodge off from the nearest town, leaving six people with reasons to want Soren silenced.
key_evidence: The hallway camera, synchronized to the lodge network clock, shows Tamsin Roe continuously in the dining hall from 10:02:10 to 10:05:40, while the coroner places Soren's death at approximately 10:04. The recording is stored on an isolated backup drive and has no gaps or signs of editing.

Gideon Wren.motive: Soren had learned Gideon was selling confidential company schedules to a rival.

Nessa Quill.relationship_to_victim: Soren's former doctoral student and current research lead
Nessa Quill.motive: Soren intended to patent Nessa's private research under his own name and terminate her contract.

Orin Vale.motive: Soren had cut Orin out of the company and threatened to expose his embezzlement of travel funds.

title: The Lake House Bolt
background: The Vey family gathers at their aging lake house to celebrate the retirement of its owner, Gideon Vey, whose plan to sell the property has divided the family. At 10:20 p.m., Gideon is found dead in the locked study, struck once with a brass boat cleat from the mantel. A storm has cut the road and disabled the house telephone, leaving everyone present trapped until morning.
key_evidence: The study door's interior bolt was engaged at 9:52 p.m., and its only window was painted shut with an unbroken strip of brittle sealant; the housekeeper's contemporaneous photograph confirms both conditions before the body was discovered. No one could have entered or left the study after that time without breaking the seal or opening the door from inside.

Maris Vey.motive: Gideon planned to sell the lake house, which would destroy the commission and inheritance she expected.

Theo Vey.role: Gideon's younger son and an indebted boat mechanic
Theo Vey.motive: Gideon had refused to cover Theo's gambling debts and was preparing to expose his thefts from the family business.

Nella Vey.role: Gideon's former wife and family archivist
Nella Vey.motive: Gideon intended to sell letters that could publicly disgrace Nella and jeopardize her academic career.

Ivo Vey.role: Gideon's nephew and an electrical engineer
Ivo Vey.motive: Gideon had discovered Ivo was secretly diverting money from a charitable foundation he managed.

Sera Vey.role: Gideon's youngest daughter and a documentary filmmaker
Sera Vey.motive: Gideon threatened to disinherit Sera after learning she had secretly filmed and sold footage of the family.

Calder Rusk.motive: The sale would leave Calder homeless, and Gideon had recently accused him of stealing antiques.

title: The Lantern on Stillwater
background: The Vey family gathers at their neglected lake house to celebrate patriarch Edmund Vey's seventieth birthday. During a storm-induced blackout, Edmund is found dead in the locked map room, apparently struck with a brass compass from his own collection. The room's only visible door is bolted from the inside, and the family insists nobody could have reached him after the lights failed.
key_evidence: The lake house's continuously recording hallway camera shows the map-room corridor empty from 9:41 p.m. until 9:56 p.m.; an independent medical examiner places Edmund's fatal blow at approximately 9:49 p.m. This rules out anyone reaching the map room through its visible door during the murder window.

Mara Vey.motive: Edmund had discovered that she was secretly selling family property and threatened to cut her out of his will.

Jonah Vey.role: Edmund's estranged son and marina mechanic
Jonah Vey.motive: Edmund refused to forgive Jonah for a boating accident that injured Jonah's younger brother and planned to sell the marina Jonah depended on.

Celeste Vey.role: Edmund's second wife and amateur botanist
Celeste Vey.motive: Edmund had recently begun divorce proceedings and intended to expose her forged medical records.

Iris Vey.motive: Edmund had blocked her inheritance after learning she was using his name to secure loans.

Nolan Price.motive: Edmund had found evidence that Nolan had siphoned money from the family trust.

Rhea Bell.role: Edmund's niece and caretaker of the lake house
Rhea Bell.motive: Edmund planned to evict Rhea and sell the house, despite her believing he had promised it to her.

title: The Last Lantern
background: The Ashmere family gathers at their aging lake house for the first reunion since its founder, Gideon Ashmere, placed the property in a contested trust. During a storm, Gideon is found dead beneath the boathouse lantern, apparently struck with a brass oarlock. The power fails moments later, leaving the family trapped until morning.
key_evidence: A battery-powered security camera facing the kitchen records Celia Ashmere entering at 9:20 p.m. and remaining there until 9:27 p.m.; its timestamp was independently synchronized with the county emergency radio signal. The boathouse lantern went out at 9:21 p.m., and Gideon's death occurred during that interval.

Celia Ashmere.role: Gideon's eldest daughter and trustee of the family estate
Celia Ashmere.motive: Gideon had discovered she was secretly selling heirlooms to cover gambling debts and planned to remove her from the trust.

Marcus Ashmere.role: Gideon's younger son and a disgraced former architect
Marcus Ashmere.motive: Gideon refused to finance Marcus's failing restoration business and intended to sell the lake house.

Iris Vale.role: Family historian and Gideon's longtime companion
Iris Vale.motive: Gideon had recently ended their relationship and threatened to expose that Iris had forged several family records.

Theo Ashmere.role: Gideon's grandson and caretaker of the lake house
Theo Ashmere.motive: Gideon planned to dismiss Theo after learning he had been renting the boathouse secretly to vacationers.

Nadia Frost.role: Environmental lawyer representing the lake association
Nadia Frost.motive: Gideon was about to reveal that Nadia had accepted a bribe connected to a disputed shoreline development.

Owen Bell.role: Local antique dealer invited to appraise the estate
Owen Bell.motive: Gideon had evidence that Owen replaced valuable antiques with convincing fakes and was preparing to report him.

statements.Celia Ashmere: At 9:19 p.m., I entered the kitchen, where the security camera recorded me settling in before the storm worsened. I remained there until 9:27 and did not go to the boathouse or touch the brass oarlock.
statements.Marcus Ashmere: At 9:08 p.m., I was upstairs repairing a broken cufflink in the bathroom, then at 9:20 I was in the west bedroom calling my business lender. His call record confirms we spoke while the storm shook the house.
statements.Iris Vale: At 9:08 p.m., I was in the library burning old correspondence in the fireplace, and at 9:20 I was on the front porch speaking with the family’s driver. He can confirm that our conversation continued through the worst of the rain.
statements.Theo Ashmere: At 9:08 p.m., I was in the generator shed restarting the fuel pump, and at 9:20 I was on the lakeside dock checking the mooring lines. The wet ropes and my muddy boots show that I stayed outside during the blackout.
statements.Nadia Frost: At 9:08 p.m., I was in the dining room photographing the disputed shoreline maps, and at 9:20 I was in the pantry searching for candles. The photographs retain their timestamps, and I found the candle box beside the shelves.
statements.Owen Bell: At 9:08 p.m., I was in the guest room inventorying the silverware, and at 9:20 I was in the garage examining the cracked display cabinet. My inventory notes and the cabinet’s fresh inspection marks place me there during the power failure.
